question.leadin: This person was given command of the 7th Panzer Division, which earned the nickname "Ghost Division" under his command.
question.text: Name this Nazi general who lead the North Africa Corps and was nicknamed the "Desert Fox"
question.clue: This man was allowed to commit suicide, rather than face trial, after being implicated in Claus von Stauffenberg's ("klaus von stow-fehn-behrg's") July 20th plot.

swap.leadin: This man refused to recant his writings at the Diet of Worms.
swap.text: Name this German theologian, who, angered by the Catholic Church's use of indulgences, launched the Protestant Reformation by publishing his Ninety-FIve Theses.
swap.clue: This individual also responded to "The Diatribe Concerning Human Freedom" by Erasmus with The Bondage of the Will.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about Beer Hall Putsch.
question.text: The Beer Hall Putsch happened in this city. This capital of Bavaria was also the site of the 1972 Summer Olympics, where 12 Israeli athletes were murdered.
question.clue: That used in Rollerball is the BMW Headquarters and Museum.

swap.text: The Weimar Republic was almost overthrown in this unsuccessful 1923 coup d'etat, which led to the imprisonment of Adolf Hitler.
swap.answer: Beer Hall Putsch or Munich Putsch
swap.clue: In the aftermath of this event, Georg Neithardt sentenced its main perpetrator to only 8 months in prison after being impressed by his oratory skills, which led to Erich Ludendorff's acquittal.

question.leadin: The father of this man forced him to watch the execution of his friend after trying to escape the royal court.
question.text: Identify this enlightened despot who fought the 7 Year's War against Austria.
question.clue: This ruler preemptively invaded Saxony to start a war in which his country was saved by the Miracle of the House of Brandenburg.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about an Iron Chancellor.
swap.text: One major step towards unification was Prussian victory in the Seven Weeks War against Austria, which saw a decisive Prussian victory at this battle. The Prussians used breech-loading rifles and there was a forced march by Crown Prince Frederick.
swap.clue: At this 19th-century battle, a commander pioneered his strategy of "cauldron warfare" that he later expounded upon in his Instructions for Large-Unit Commanders.

question.leadin: During this event, Gail Halvorsen was nicknamed the "Candy Bomber" because he dropped packages of candy attached to miniature parachutes.
question.text: Name this event dubbed "Operation Vittles" in which American and British planes flew supplies into Tempelhof Airport to circumvent a Soviet Blockade.
question.clue: This event was orchestrated by Curtis LeMay, who utilized C-54 Skymasters to deliver 5,000 tons of supplies a day at its climax.

swap.leadin: Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me a few more times before I notice. answer the following about Nazi Germany and the era of appeasement.
swap.text: This area of western Germany had been demilitarized under articles 42 and 44 of the Treaty of Versailles and the Treaty of Locarno. On March 7, 1936, Hitler ordered its re-occupation by military forces as a diplomatic test of will against France and Great Britain. It is named after a certain river of that region.
swap.clue: This region, reunified by the Peace of Pressburg, was led by Karl Theodor von Dalberg as Prince-Primate.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about European crusades against Baltic paganism.
question.text: This group of Germanic knights, founded during the Third Crusade, launched several crusades against Lithuanian pagans. They were defeated at the first battle of Grunwald, or Tannenberg.
question.answerHtml: Teutonic Knights [or Teutonic Order; or Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem; or Deutscher Ritter-Orden; do not accept or prompt on "Knights Hospitallers"]
question.clue: It was headquartered in Marienburg for the most successful part of its history, and was notably defeated at Lake Peipus by Alexander Nevsky.

swap.text: The 1914 Battle of Tannenberg saw Germany defeat Russia under the command of this general. From 1916 to the end of World War I, he effectively shared power with Erich Ludendorff.
swap.clue: This man was reviled by Hitler, who referred to him as "that old fool" and "that old reactionary" during his time as president of the Weimar ] Republic.

question.text: Named for a German field marshal, this plan involved defeating France in six weeks, before Russia could mobilize. This plan was carried out poorly by Helmuth von Moltke the Younger.
question.clue: According to this plan, the German army aimed to defeat France before focusing on Russia through rapid military action through Belgium.

swap.leadin: Alfred Thayer Mahan's magnum opus attributed large aspects of Great Britain's general dominance of the world to the strength of its military branch of this type.
swap.text: Name this broad branch of a country's armed forces that may include destroyers and cruisers. The advent of the HMS Dreadnought completely changed how power within these military branches was viewed.
swap.answerHtml: navy [accept maritime force; prompt on ships, boats, or other more specific watercraft]
swap.clue: Taisho Japan signed the Five-Power Washington Treaty to disarm these forces. All-rice diets caused beriberi ("BAIR-ee-BAIR-ee") in Meiji Japan's force of this kind, which was modernized with ironclads and dreadnoughts.

question.leadin: Name these poets who took prominent roles in European politics.
question.text: This poet, regarded as the second-most famous European behind Napoleon in his life, maintained a public stance of skepticism against German nationalism through the Napoleonic Wars. He also wrote Faust.
question.clue: This writer described Kellermann's charge with the words "a new epoch in the history of the world has begun." This writer contributed such German classics as Faust and The Sorrows of Young Werther.

swap.leadin: One member of this family secretly purchased the captured crown jewels of Charles the Bold from the city of Basel.
swap.text: Name this German banking family based in Augsburg which reached its height under Jakob and dominated European business during the 15th and 16th centuries.
swap.clue: Archduke Sigismund granted a member of this family control over Tyrol's silver mines after that member of this family loaned Sigismund a huge number of florins.

question.leadin: The Catholic theologian August Rohling drew on the Orientalist Johann Andreas Eisenmenger to justify this ideology.
question.text: Name this ideology propounded by nineteenth-century cultural pessimists like Julius Langbehn. It was famously expressed in an Heinrich von Treitschke essay which claimed that a certain people were 'our misfortune'.
question.answerHtml: antisemitism [accept Judaeophobia, anti-Jewish racism and other obvious equivalents; prompt on racism]

swap.leadin: This hymn is basically a paraphrase of Psalm 46.
swap.text: Give the English title or first line of this hymn, still sung today even though it was written in 1529. This hymn proclaims that the Lord is "a bulwark never failing" and is "our helper... amid the flood of mortal ills prevailing."
swap.answer: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God

question.leadin: Answer the following about historically epic European parties.
question.text: A moonlight picnic with male dancers and the sodomization of a swan may have happened on any given night at the castle Neuschwanstein, built by this reputedly mad German king who patronized Richard Wagner.
question.clue: This "mad king" who is perhaps best known for his patronage of Richard Wagner.

swap.leadin: Its first ruler was Otto of Scheyern, who in 1124 moved his family to their namesake castle on the Paar.
swap.text: Name this German noble house, which ruled Bavaria from 1180 until 1918.
swap.clue: Joseph II seized on the 1778 death of a member of this house to occupy their territory, only to be forced to withdraw by Frederick the Great in the Treaty of Teschen.

question.leadin: A group of people from this polity were dumped in a squalid camp in Blackheath before being shipped off to work in naval stores in the Hudson Valley.
question.text: Daniel Defoe advocated for "poor" people from what polity during a 1700s refugee crisis? James I married off his daughter Elizabeth Stuart to a ruler of this polity who was made King of Bohemia in 1619.
question.answerHtml: the Palatinate [or Electoral Palatinate, Electorate of the Palatinate, Pfalz, Kurpfalz, or Rhineland-Palatinate; accept Poor Palatines or Elector Palatine]

swap.leadin: Goethe's dramatic rendition of his life has him say the phrase "Kiss my ass" when he told it to the Bishop of Bamberg.
swap.text: Identify this German hero and mercenary that is known for fighting in the Peasants War against the Holy Roman Emperor. He had a prosthetic hand.
swap.clue: This play about an iron-armed soldier whose nemesis Weislingen has him arrested. Weislingen is eventually poisoned on the orders of the beautiful Adelheid.
